The math behind choicer: hierarchical Bayesian multinomial probit

Source: vignettes/articles/hierarchical_mnp_math.Rmd
hierarchical_mnp_math.Rmd

This document describes the hierarchical Bayesian multinomial probit with i.i.d. shocks (HMNP) as implemented in src/hmnprobit.cpp, with shared infrastructure in src/hb_internal.h. The R-side entry point is run_hmnprobit(). The hierarchical structure (βi∼N(b,W)\beta_i \sim N(b, W); δj=zj′θ+ξj\delta_j = z_j'\theta + \xi_j) is identical to the HMNL (see the companion article); this note focuses on what differs: the shock family, the data augmentation, identification, and the parallelization asymmetry.

Notation

As in the HMNL article, plus: UijtU_{ijt} the latent utilities (augmented data), UiotU_{iot} the per-task outside latent, σ2\sigma^2 the (non-identified) common shock variance, Gi=Xi′XiG_i = X_i'X_i the respondent Gram block.

1. Model Definition

Uijt=xijt′βi+δj+εijt,Uiot=εiot,ε∼i.i.d. N(0,σ2),U_{ijt} = x_{ijt}'\beta_i + \delta_j + \varepsilon_{ijt}, \qquad U_{iot} = \varepsilon_{iot}, \qquad \varepsilon \sim \text{i.i.d. } N(0, \sigma^2),

with choice by argmax within the task including the outside latent. The outside option is stochastic — its own shock on top of systematic utility 0, not a deterministic bound. This keeps the model structurally parallel to the HMNL (whose outside good necessarily carries an EV1 shock): utilities differenced against the outside are equicorrelated (Var⁡=2σ2\operatorname{Var} = 2\sigma^2, Cov⁡=σ2\operatorname{Cov} = \sigma^2), the exact probit analog of logit-with-outside-good, and it is what makes the π/6\pi/\sqrt6 scale comparison between the two models meaningful.

The sampler works in un-differenced utility space: with i.i.d. shocks the latent conditionals are univariate normals whose only coupling is the argmax truncation, unbalanced choice sets are trivial, and there is no error covariance matrix to sample — one scalar σ2\sigma^2. Respondent coefficients are normal only (βi∼N(b,W)\beta_i \sim N(b, W); a log-normal coordinate would break conjugacy), and the alternative level is exactly the HMNL’s: δj=zj′θ+ξj\delta_j = z_j'\theta + \xi_j, ξj∼N(0,σd2)\xi_j \sim N(0, \sigma_d^2).

2. Identification

  • Scale. The likelihood is invariant to a common rescaling of (U,σ)(U, \sigma). The chain runs on the non-identified parameterization (free σ2\sigma^2 — parameter expansion, which mixes better than pinning σ2=1\sigma^2 = 1), and every kept draw is normalized by the matching power of the current σ\sigma: reported b/σb/\sigma, W/σ2W/\sigma^2, δ/σ\delta/\sigma, θ/σ\theta/\sigma, σd2/σ2\sigma_d^2/\sigma^2, βi/σ\beta_i/\sigma. This is the McCulloch–Rossi σ11\sigma_{11} discipline: identified summaries are computed on per-draw-normalized chains, never by normalizing posterior means (E[b/σ]≠E[b]/E[σ]E[b/\sigma] \ne E[b]/E[\sigma]). Raw chains are kept in draws$*_raw.
  • Location. As in the HMNL, the outside option anchors the level of δ\delta; version 1 requires it.
  • Degenerate cross-check. With one inside alternative (J=1J = 1) the model is a binary probit whose composite error ε1−εo\varepsilon_1 - \varepsilon_o has variance 2σ22\sigma^2, so the identified coefficients equal 2\sqrt2 times the glm(..., binomial(link = "probit")) coefficients — a closed-form validation used in the test suite.

3. Priors and Joint Posterior

As in the HMNL for (b,W,θ,σd2)(b, W, \theta, \sigma_d^2), plus σ2∼ℐ𝒢(a0,s0)\sigma^2 \sim \mathcal{IG}(a_0, s_0) (defaults a0=s0=3a_0 = s_0 = 3) on the non-identified variance. All conditionals below are conjugate — the sampler has no Metropolis steps.

4. The Gibbs Sampler

One systematic-scan iteration:

(a) Fused respondent pass (work-shared over respondents): for each task, a truncated-normal sweep over the inside rows and the outside latent in fixed order — the chosen latent is drawn on (max⁡others,∞)(\max \text{others}, \infty), every other latent on (−∞,Uchosen)(-\infty, U_{\text{chosen}}), each conditional a plain N(mean,σ2)N(\text{mean}, \sigma^2) with mean x′βi+δjx'\beta_i + \delta_j (or 0 for the outside latent, which participates exactly like a row and enters the bounds at its current value). Then the conjugate βi\beta_i regression draw on the δ\delta-residualized utilities,

βi∣⋅∼N(Qi−1ri,Qi−1),Qi=W−1+Gi/σ2,ri=W−1b+Xi′(Ui−δ)/σ2,\beta_i \mid \cdot \sim N\big(Q_i^{-1} r_i,\; Q_i^{-1}\big), \qquad Q_i = W^{-1} + G_i/\sigma^2, \qquad r_i = W^{-1} b + X_i'(U_i - \delta)/\sigma^2,

with Gi=Xi′XiG_i = X_i'X_i precomputed once; then a refresh of the row cache μx(r)=xr′βi\mu_x(r) = x_r'\beta_i.

(b) δj\delta_j — work-shared conjugate draws. Given the augmented UU, the δj\delta_j are conditionally independent across jj (the softmax coupling of the HMNL does not exist here), so the draws parallelize validly:

δj∣⋅∼N(∑r∈j(Ur−μx(r))/σ2+zj′θ/σd2nj/σ2+1/σd2,(nj/σ2+1/σd2)−1),\delta_j \mid \cdot \sim N\left(\frac{\sum_{r \in j}(U_r - \mu_x(r))/\sigma^2 + z_j'\theta/\sigma_d^2}{n_j/\sigma^2 + 1/\sigma_d^2},\; \big(n_j/\sigma^2 + 1/\sigma_d^2\big)^{-1}\right),

each jj’s sufficient statistic summed over its CSR row list in fixed row order by a single thread (bitwise thread-count invariance).

(c) RSS pass (work-shared, fixed order) with the new β\beta and δ\delta — a separate pass so σ2\sigma^2 conditions on current values, not the stale δ\delta from (a). Outside latents contribute Uiot2U_{iot}^2 (their residual is the latent itself) and count in nlatentsn_{\text{latents}}.

(d) Hierarchy (master): bb, WW, θ\theta, (σd2,ad)(\sigma_d^2, a_d) exactly as in the HMNL, then

σ2∣U,β,δ∼ℐ𝒢(a0+12nlatents,s0+12RSS).\sigma^2 \mid U, \beta, \delta \sim \mathcal{IG}\big(a_0 + \tfrac12 n_{\text{latents}},\; s_0 + \tfrac12 \text{RSS}\big).

Recording. Raw chains for (b,W,δ,θ,σd2,σ2)(b, W, \delta, \theta, \sigma_d^2, \sigma^2); the βi/δ/ξ\beta_i / \delta / \xi summaries are accumulated on the identified scale (divided by the current σ\sigma) at recording time.

5. Sampling Primitives

The truncated-normal draw is the three-regime sampler in src/bayes_samplers.h (naive rejection / Robert exponential rejection / inverse-CDF), drawing exclusively from per-(iteration, unit) Xoshiro256++ streams. The worker-side βi\beta_i draw uses the hand-rolled Cholesky machinery of src/hb_internal.h with per-thread scratch — never BLAS/LAPACK off the master thread.

6. Post-Processing and Reported Quantities

As for the HMNL, with two differences. Choice probabilities have no closed form; with i.i.d. shocks they reduce to the 1-D integral

P(j)=∫ϕ(u)∏k≠jΦ(Vj−Vk+u)du(Vo=0,identified scale σ=1),P(j) = \int \phi(u) \prod_{k \ne j} \Phi(V_j - V_k + u)\, du \qquad (V_o = 0,\ \text{identified scale } \sigma = 1),

evaluated by fixed-node Gauss–Hermite quadrature in predict.choicer_hb() (deterministic; verified against brute-force Monte Carlo argmax). And logsum() / consumer_surplus() refuse with an informative error: the logsum formula is EV1-specific, probit E[max⁡U]E[\max U] has no closed form, and the simulated-Emax variant is roadmapped — the HMNL is the welfare workhorse.

7. Implementation Details

Same engine contract, persistent-region structure, abort protocol, and thread-invariance discipline as the HMNL (see its §7). The RNG partition adds tag N+iN + i for respondent ii’s βi\beta_i regression draw; the master block remains based at 2N+J2N + J (σd2\sigma_d^2 and σ2\sigma^2 share the last tag’s stream in fixed order). The fused pass writes only respondent-owned slots (UU, UoutU_{\text{out}}, μx\mu_x, βi\beta_i column, RSS slot), the δ\delta pass only δj\delta_j, and the RSS reduction happens on the master thread in fixed respondent order.

  • McCulloch, R., & Rossi, P. E. (1994). An exact likelihood analysis of the multinomial probit model. Journal of Econometrics, 64(1–2), 207–240.
  • Rossi, P. E., Allenby, G. M., & McCulloch, R. (2005). Bayesian Statistics and Marketing. Wiley.
  • Train, K. (2009). Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.
